part.text: All scenarios now behave consistently. Final diff:

Fixed in `lib/adapters/http.js:170`.

**Root cause:** When the effective `maxBodyLength` was `-1` (axios's unlimited default), the adapter omitted the option entirely, so `follow-redirects` silently applied its own 10MB default — but only when redirects were enabled (plain `http/https` with `maxRedirects: 0` never enforced a limit), producing the inconsistent behavior from the issue.

**Fix:** Always forward `maxBodyLength` to the transport options, mapping `-1` to `Infinity` (since `follow-redirects` would otherwise reject every write with `data.length <= -1`).

**Validation:**
- `should support max body length` and `should properly support default max body length (follow-redirects as well)` (the FAIL_TO_PASS case) both pass.
- Full `test/unit/adapters/http.js`: 56 passing, 2 failing — both failures (`max content length`, `HTTPS protocol`) also fail on the unmodified baseline (environment issues).
- All 4 issue repro scenarios (`default`, `maxBodyLength: -1`, `maxRedirects: 0`, `maxBodyLength: Infinity`) with a 20MB body now succeed consistently, while an explicit small limit (`maxBodyLength: 2000`) is still enforced.
